Eligible  Divisions:  Secondary  &  Postsecondary/  Collegiate  
Round  One:  50  Q  test  (60  minutes)  Digital  Upload:  NO  
Solo  Event:  1  competitor    
 
New  for  2026-2027

Policy
 
Research
 
website

topics
 
have
 
been
 
clariﬁed.
  
Event  Summary
 World  Health  and  Disparities  allows  members  to  gain  knowledge  and  skills  regarding  world  health  and  disparities.  This  
competitive
 
event
 
consists
 
of
 
a
 
written
 
test. In  the  event  of  a  tie,  the  essay  will  be  judged  to  break  the  tie.  The  event  aims  to  
increase
 
competence
 
in
 
understanding
 
world
 
health
 
and
 
identifying
 
and
 
overcoming
 
health
 
disparities.
                                                             
General  Event  Information
 
General  Rules   Competitors  must  be  familiar  with  and  adhere  to  the  General  Rules  and  Regulations.  
Dress  Code  Proper  business  attire  or  ofﬁcial  HOSA  uniform.  Bonus  points  will  be  awarded  for  proper  dress.  
Competitors  Must  Provide  ●  Photo  ID ●  Two  #2  lead  pencils  (not  mechanical)  with  an  eraser  ●  Neon  colored  foam  earplugs,  NOT  earbuds,  for  noise  control  (optional)  HOSA  Conference  Staff  will  provide  equipment  and  supplies  listed  in  Appendix  I.  
Ofﬁcial  References   The  references  below  are  used  in  the  development  of  the  test  questions.   Content  is  posted  as  of  September  1,  2026:   ●  Barr,  Donald  A.   Health  Disparities  in  the  US .  Johns  Hopkins  University  Press,  Latest  edition. ●  Our  World  in  Data  website ●  National  Institute  of  Minority  Health  &  Disparities: https://www.nimhd.nih.gov/   ●  World  Health  Organization.  Health  Equity:  https://www.who.int/health-topics/health-equity#tab=tab_1 (Fact  Sheets  and  Questions  &  Answers  sections)  ●  Selected  featured  topics  of  the  KFF  Independent  Source  for  Health  Policy  Research  website,  including  Health  Policy  101,  Employer  Health  Beneﬁts  Survey,  Health  System  Tracker,  Global  Health  Policy,   Health  Costs,  Racial  Equality  and  Health  Policy  and  the  Uninsured  and  State  Health  Facts: https://www.kff.org/policy-research/ (see  test  plan).  
 ROUND  ONE-  Test
 
Test  Instructions  All  competitors  will  be  given  a  test  and  test  answer  sheet.  The  written  test  will  consist  of  50  multiple  choice  questions  in  a  maximum  of  60  minutes.  See  test  instructions  here. An  essay  tiebreaker  question  will  be  administered  with  the  original  test.   Essay  tiebreakers  will  be  completed  on  the  back  of  the  test  answer  sheet.  
 World  Health  &  Disparities   ILC  Guidelines  (September  2026)         Page  1  of  2  The  expectation  is  that  competitors  read  and  are  aware  of  all  the  content  within  these  guidelines  and  associated  links.  Successful  competitors  will  study  all  links  for  the  detailed  information.   

Time  Remaining  Announcements  
There  will  be  NO  verbal  announcements  for  time  remaining  during  ILC  testing.  All  ILC  testing  will  be  completed  in  the  Testing  Center,  and  competitors  are  responsible  for  monitoring  their  own  time.  
Written  Test  Plan  The  test  plan  for  the  World  Health  and  Disparities  Test  is:  ●  What  is  Health  -  20%  ●  Health  Disparities  &  Diversity  -  40%  ●  Disparities  in  Treatment  &  Medical  Decisions  -  20%  ●  Reducing  Health  Disparities  -  20%  
Sample  Test  Questions  1.  What  medical  condition  has  been  impacted  by  a  phone-based  intervention  program  with  the  Navajo  patients?            https://www.nimhd.nih.gov/news-events/research-spotlight/home-based-phone-intervention-improved-uptake-recommended-medical A.  Diabetes  B.  Parkinson's  C.  Heart  Failure  D.  ALS  2.  According  to  2016-2017  OECD  data,  which  of  the  following  countries  has  the  lowest  infant  mortality  rate?   (Barr  pp  3)  A.  United  States  B.  Japan C.  Switzerland  D.  Canada  3.  According  to  the  WHO,  how  many  years  could  be  added  to  a  person’s  life  expectancy  if  primary  care  interventions  were  increased  in  low  and  middle-income  countries?    https://www.who.int/health-topics/health-equity#tab=tab_1 A.    2.4  years  B.    2.7  years  C.    3.4  years  D.    3.7  years  
 Final  Scoring 
 In  the  event  of  a  tie,  the  essay  will  be  judged  to  break  the  tie.    
Future  Opportunities   The  HOSA  Scholarship  program  has  funding  available  for  HOSA  members  who  have  an  interest  in  various  health  careers!   The  application  process  begins  January  1,  2027,  and  can  be  found  here: https://hosa.org/scholarships/.   Graduating  from  high  school  or  completing  your  postsecondary/collegiate  program  does  not  mean  your  HOSA  journey  has  to  
end.
